correctness.rationale: The Fock monomial basis proves the exact positive Szegő-Gram Rayleigh quotient. Distinct finite Vandermonde columns ensure strict positivity. Exact rational Hardy cardinal interpolants represent the inverse kernel Gram and, after scaling, converge in H² because all poles remain uniformly outside the closed unit disk. An inner Blaschke factor supplies the required exact Hardy norm. Consequently the rescaled inverse normalized Gram converges in finite-matrix norm to (1−|a|²)^(2N−2)ww*, whose unique nonzero eigenvalue yields the stated sharp constant and minimizer line. The cyclic Fourier calculation gives the roots-of-unity identity for all N and 0<epsilon<1. Standalone 85-digit numerical verification passed 88 assertions, supplementary only.

value.rationale: For the natural quantitative no-cancellation invariant of N compact Fock dilation operators, the result identifies the precise loss of stability as the distinct symbols approach a common interior slope. The arbitrary-complex-direction constant records configuration geometry; the optimal coefficient line specifies the worst cancellation, and the exact Fourier family supplies a global benchmark. These address a motivated gap in fixed-symbol comparison theorems and are not mere membership criteria, coefficient rescalings or numerical examples.
